hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the right side of the image.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Calming
hazards.description: The wide, unmarked asphalt surface may encourage higher vehicle speeds in a residential area.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures sightlines between pedestrians attempting to cross and oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Overgrown Vegetation
hazards.description: Dense bushes on the left side of the image may obstruct sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground, adjacent to the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Lane Markings
hazards.description: The absence of painted lane lines can lead to unpredictable vehicle positioning and higher speeds on a wide roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, on the asphalt surface

hazards.name: Unmarked wide roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide road can lead to higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

hazards.name: Missing sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a clear, paved pedestrian walkway, forcing people to walk in the road or on unpaved surfaces.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street behind the fence

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: Visible cracking and wear in the asphalt surface can affect vehicle handling and create tripping hazards if pedestrians cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and foreground of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The narrow sidewalk is directly adjacent to the curb with no planting strip or physical barrier separating pedestrians from parked or moving vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk area in front of the row houses

hazards.name: Roadway Debris
hazards.description: A cardboard box or similar debris is present in the travel lane, which could cause sudden vehicle swerving.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line throughout the frame

hazards.name: Sidewalk Encroachment
hazards.description: Residential stairs and trash bins narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk in front of the row houses

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian crossings
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are visible, requiring pedestrians to cross a wide street without any designated protection or priority.
hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible street length

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground where the silver car is parked.

hazards.name: Uneven Sidewalk Surface
hazards.description: Cracks and minor debris on the sidewalk create potential tripping hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Visible on the sidewalk surface in the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Vegetation Overgrowth
hazards.description: Weeds and vegetation are encroaching on the sidewalk space on the right side of the image.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk is very narrow and constrained by building stairs, making it difficult for two people to pass or for users with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Roadway Potholes
hazards.description: Significant potholes and cracking in the asphalt can cause tripping hazards for pedestrians crossing or lead to erratic vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Poor pavement condition
hazards.description: Significant cracking and degradation of the roadway surface can create tripping hazards and affect vehicle control.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the foreground and midground roadway

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Building stairs, trash cans, and overgrown vegetation encroach on the narrow walking path.

hazards.name: Visibility obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No street light poles are visible in the immediate vicinity, which may create safety concerns after dark.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A wide curb cut for the industrial garage creates a large area where vehicles may cross the pedestrian path without clear demarcation.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: The long, windowless wall of the garage reduces natural surveillance and creates a less inviting environment for walking.
hazards.location_in_image: The grey building on the right half of the image.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce the crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossings with high-visibility paint to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical speed control measures to reduce vehicle speeds to levels appropriate for a residential street.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at the intersection to ensure accessibility for all users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway, while also narrowing the perceived street width.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer/Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to increase physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Pavement Markings
interventions.description: Apply high-visibility lane markings and a center line to organize traffic flow and narrow the perceived width of the travel lanes.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove overgrown vegetation to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Lane Striping and Narrowing
interventions.description: Add lane markings to define travel lanes and reduce the perceived width of the road, which helps slow traffic.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a dense residential street.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Vegetation
interventions.description: Add street trees to provide a visual buffer between the sidewalk and the road, which also helps to naturally slow traffic by narrowing the driver's field of vision.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to create a physical and psychological buffer between the walkway and the roadway.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points to ensure clear sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps or Cushions
interventions.description: Implement vertical traffic calming measures to ensure vehicle speeds remain low and consistent with a residential environment.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add paint to define travel and parking lanes, narrowing the perceived roadway to encourage slower driving.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lighting to improve visibility and perceived safety during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Markings
interventions.description: Paint lane lines to define the travel way and narrow the effective width of the street to slow traffic.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widening the sidewalk to meet modern accessibility standards would improve pedestrian flow and safety.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair potholes and resurface the street to provide a safe, level surface for all users.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and repave the degraded roadway to improve the surface for all users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Maintenance and Clearing
interventions.description: Ensure a clear, unobstructed path of travel by managing building encroachments and vegetation.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Install street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implementing speed humps or curb extensions would help manage vehicle speeds on this residential block.

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation or Narrowing
interventions.description: Narrow the driveway apron or use contrasting materials to clearly define the pedestrian right-of-way across the garage entrance.
